title: The Hook: A Long Journey!
text: Imagine you want to visit your grandparents who live very far away. If you walk, it might take many days! But if you sit in a magical metal box with wheels, you can reach there in just a few hours. Have you ever wondered what these 'magical boxes' are?

title: Socratic Thinking: Think About It...
text: Why can't we just walk everywhere? What happens if you want to cross a huge river or an ocean? How did people travel before cars and trains were invented?

content.title: Discovery: Moving Things Around
content.description: Watch how a horse cart moves slowly, but a train zooms past! Over time, humans invented different machines with wheels to travel faster.

title: The Reveal: What is Transportation?
text: The movement of people or goods from one place to another is called Transportation (Parivahan). The machines we use for this, like cars, buses, and trains, are called Vehicles. Long ago, ancient Indians used chariots (Rath) and bullock carts!

content.question: Which of the following is NOT a vehicle?

content.title: Reflection: Reflect & Share
content.text: Close your eyes and think about your favourite vehicle. Why do you like it? Tell your younger sibling or friend about the last time you travelled in it.

content.title: Connection: Connecting the Dots
content.text: Did you know? The invention of the wheel changed everything! It connects to our ancient history where wooden wheels were first used on carts. Without the wheel, most vehicles today wouldn't exist.

content.title: Mastery: Mini Challenge
content.text: Draw a picture of a vehicle that uses animal power (like a bullock cart) and another vehicle that uses an engine (like a car). Label them!

title: The Hook: The Three Paths
text: If you are a bird, you can fly. If you are a fish, you can swim. If you are a cheetah, you can run! But humans don't have wings or gills. Yet, we can travel through the sky, across oceans, and over mountains. How?

title: Socratic Thinking: What would you choose?
text: If you have to travel to another country across the sea, would you take a bus or a ship? Why do you think a train cannot travel on water?

content.title: Discovery: Land, Water, and Air
content.description: Notice how cars use roads (Land), ships float on oceans (Water), and airplanes fly in the sky (Air)!

title: The Reveal: The Modes of Transport
text: There are three main modes of transport: 1. Land Transport: Vehicles moving on roads and tracks (Cars, Trains). 2. Water Transport: Vehicles moving on water (Boats, Ships). 3. Air Transport: Vehicles flying in the sky (Airplanes, Helicopters).

content.question: Which of these is an example of water transport?

content.title: Reflection: Wait, is it Land or Water?
content.text: Some students think a hovercraft is only a water vehicle. Actually, it can travel over land, water, mud, and ice! But generally, boats and ships are strictly water transport.

title: Connection: Emergency Vehicles
text: Transportation connects to our safety, too! Ambulances and fire engines are special land vehicles that save lives. When we see them, we should always make way.

content.title: Mastery: Become an Explorer!
content.text: Look outside your window or walk down your street safely. Count how many different modes of transport you can spot in 5 minutes. Classify them into Land, Water, or Air!
